newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil gang steals $5 million in gold, jewels.
newsitem.headline: Brazil gang steals $5 million in gold, jewels.

text.p: Thieves in Brazil stole gold and jewels worth an estimated $5 million after kidnapping a string of bank officials and their relatives and breaking into a huge store of pawned goods, a bank official said on Monday.

The raid began on Friday evening when the manager of the Caixa Economica Federal mortgage bank in the Amazonian city of Belem was handcuffed while shopping and forced into a car by six men posing as police officers, bank superintendent Guilherme Bacellar said.

The robbers demanded the manager open the safe but discovered they also needed to kidnap the bank's treasurer, who carried the key. The gang raided the treasurer's home only to find he was in church. His wife was taken hostage before the treasurer was grabbed after the service, Bacellar said.

Finally, with several relatives of the two men being held at gunpoint, the gang broke into the safe and spent hours filling sacks with gold and jewels that had been pawned to the bank by an estimated 20,000 borrowers. The gang disappeared and was being hunted by police, the official said.
"It's not just a question of the money. Those goods have a very high sentimental value to a lot of people," Bacellar told Reuters.

A medical team was providing assistance to clients of the bank, many of whom were in shock after learning of the raid. Bacellar said the bank would reimburse borrowers for about $7.5 million, equivalent to 1 1/2 times the value of goods stolen.
